title: Password Reset Procedure
description: User cannot log in, forgot password, or account is locked out
steps: Verify user identity via employee ID and registered email.
Navigate to Active Directory → Users → Locate the account.
Click 'Reset Password' and generate a temporary secure password.
Ensure 'User must change password at next logon' is checked.
Notify user via registered email with the temporary password.
Confirm MFA (multi-factor authentication) is still active after reset.
Log resolution in ticket system with timestamp.
result: Password successfully reset. User can now log in.

title: VPN Connection Failure — Cannot Connect
description: User cannot connect to VPN at all, VPN client error, VPN connection dead, VPN not working, remote access fails to establish, VPN signal lost, no VPN bars
steps: Check if the VPN client is up-to-date — update if not.
Verify the user is connecting to the correct VPN server address.
Ask the user to disable any third-party firewall/antivirus temporarily.
Run the VPN client as Administrator.
Clear VPN client cache: go to Settings → Clear Saved Sessions.
Check VPN gateway availability from the network admin portal.
If issue persists, re-install the VPN client from the IT software portal.
result: VPN connection established successfully.

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) / System Crash
description: Computer shows blue screen, crashes, kernel panic, stop error
steps: Note the stop code displayed on the BSOD screen (e.g., MEMORY_MANAGEMENT).
Restart the machine and boot into Safe Mode.
Open Event Viewer → Windows Logs → System — check for critical errors.
Run Windows Memory Diagnostic Tool (mdsched.exe) to test RAM.
Run sfc /scannow in an elevated Command Prompt to repair system files.
Check for recent driver updates and roll back any new drivers.
If stop code relates to disk: run chkdsk /f /r on the system drive.
Escalate to hardware team if RAM or disk failure is confirmed.
result: Root cause identified; follow-up action required.
escalationReason: Possible hardware failure — L2 hardware team review needed.

title: Software Installation Request
description: User needs to install software, application not available, software request
steps: Verify software is listed in the approved IT software catalog.
Check if the user has a valid license or license is available in the pool.
Approve or deny request via the IT request management portal.
If approved, push installation via SCCM/Intune to the user's device.
Notify user when installation is complete.
Update the CMDB with the new software installation record.
result: Software installation request submitted for approval.
escalationReason: Requires IT manager approval for non-standard software.

title: Cannot Access Shared Network Drive
description: Network drive not mapped, cannot access shared folder, file server unreachable
steps: Verify user is connected to the corporate network or VPN.
Check that the network drive mapping exists: open File Explorer → This PC.
Re-map the drive: right-click This PC → Map Network Drive → enter the UNC path.
Confirm the user has permissions in Active Directory for the shared folder.
Test connectivity to the file server: ping <server-name>.
Check file server status on the infrastructure dashboard.
Submit firewall rule review request if access is still denied.
result: Network drive access restored.

title: Email Not Syncing / Outlook Issues
description: Outlook not sending or receiving emails, email sync issues, OST file corrupt
steps: Check user's internet and Exchange server connectivity.
Restart Outlook and verify the account is connected (bottom status bar).
Run Outlook in safe mode: Win+R → outlook /safe.
Rebuild the Outlook profile: Control Panel → Mail → Show Profiles → Add.
If OST file is corrupted, run scanpst.exe (Inbox Repair Tool).
Verify Exchange server status from the admin portal.
Re-activate Microsoft 365 license if activation error appears.
result: Outlook sync restored.

title: Printer Not Working
description: Printer offline, cannot print, print spooler error, printer not found
steps: Check printer power and physical cable/wireless connection.
Set the printer as the default printer: Settings → Printers & Scanners.
Clear the print queue: Services → Print Spooler → Stop → delete files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS → Restart spooler.
Remove and re-add the printer from Printers & Scanners settings.
Re-install printer drivers from the manufacturer or IT software portal.
Test printing a test page from the printer's own display.
If network printer, verify the printer IP is reachable via ping.
result: Printer connectivity restored.

title: Suspected Malware / Virus Infection
description: Malware detected, ransomware, suspicious files, antivirus alert, computer infected
steps: IMMEDIATELY disconnect the device from the corporate network (unplug LAN / disable Wi-Fi).
Do NOT shut the machine down — preserve volatile memory for forensics.
Notify the Security Operations Center (SOC) immediately via phone.
Open the endpoint security console to isolate the machine remotely.
Capture a memory dump and disk image for forensic analysis.
Initiate the Incident Response runbook (IR-SEC-001).
Reset all credentials the machine had access to from a clean device.
result: Security incident initiated. Awaiting SOC response.
escalationReason: Security incident — mandatory SOC and management escalation.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Setup / Reset
description: User lost MFA device, cannot receive OTP, MFA authenticator app not working, new phone setup
steps: Verify user identity via HR department or manager confirmation.
Admin: sign in to Azure AD / Okta → Select user → Authentication methods.
Delete the existing MFA methods for the user.
Send the user a fresh MFA registration link via a secondary verified channel.
Guide the user to re-enroll the Authenticator app on the new device.
Test login with the new MFA setup before closing the ticket.
Log the MFA reset event in the security audit trail.
result: MFA successfully reset and re-enrolled.
escalationReason: Requires identity verification — cannot be fully automated.

title: Internet Connectivity Lost — No Connection
description: No internet access at all, completely disconnected, cannot reach any website, DNS failure, IP conflict
steps: Run ipconfig /all to check IP configuration — look for APIPA (169.x.x.x) addresses.
Try ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew to get a fresh IP from DHCP.
Flush DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns.
Test basic IP connectivity: ping 8.8.8.8 (if this works, the issue is DNS not internet).
If ping to 8.8.8.8 also fails, check the network adapter and physical cable/Wi-Fi.
Restart the network adapter: Device Manager → Network Adapters → Disable/Enable.
Check if other devices on the same network are affected — if yes, escalate to network team.
Restart the router/switch if only one device is affected and physical connection is confirmed.
result: Network connectivity restored.

title: Slow Internet / Network Performance Degradation
description: Internet is slow, sluggish, laggy, high latency, intermittent connectivity, poor throughput, bandwidth issues
steps: Run a speed test (speedtest.net) to measure current throughput and compare to expected speeds.
Check for other users or applications consuming bandwidth: open Task Manager → Performance → Ethernet.
Flush DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns, then retry.
Check for Windows Updates or background downloads consuming bandwidth.
Connect via Ethernet cable instead of Wi-Fi to rule out wireless interference.
Move closer to the Wi-Fi access point if on wireless, or try a different band (5GHz vs 2.4GHz).
Check if the issue is specific to one application or all internet traffic.
If multiple users are affected, raise with the network team to check uplink utilization.
result: Network performance restored to acceptable levels.

title: Computer Running Slow / High CPU Usage
description: Laptop or desktop is very slow, high CPU or memory usage, applications freezing, sluggish response
steps: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) → identify processes consuming high CPU/memory.
End non-essential high-usage processes.
Check startup programs: Task Manager → Startup tab → Disable unnecessary items.
Run Disk Cleanup and clear temporary files.
Check for pending Windows Updates — install and restart.
Run Malwarebytes scan to rule out malware causing performance issues.
If RAM is below 8GB, submit a hardware upgrade request via the IT portal.
If SSD/HDD is over 90% full, archive old files to network storage or OneDrive.
result: Performance improved. Long-term: hardware review recommended.

title: Application Crashing or Not Opening
description: Application keeps crashing, software not responding, app fails to launch, closes unexpectedly
steps: Check Event Viewer → Application logs for the specific crash error code.
Run the application as Administrator to rule out permission issues.
Clear application cache and temp files.
Uninstall and re-install the application from the IT software portal.
Check if the application is compatible with the current OS version.
Verify that required dependencies (e.g., .NET, Visual C++ Redistributable) are installed.
Submit a bug report to the software vendor if issue persists after reinstall.
result: Application reinstalled and running normally.

title: New Employee Onboarding — Account Setup
description: New employee account creation, new user setup, create AD account, onboarding
steps: Receive approved onboarding form from HR with employee details.
Create Active Directory account with correct OU, department, and manager.
Assign Microsoft 365 license group based on job role.
Add user to appropriate security groups and distribution lists.
Provision email account and send welcome email with credentials.
Configure MFA registration and send enrollment link.
Set up laptop via Autopilot or image deployment with user profile.
Brief user on IT policies and provide IT helpdesk contact.
result: New user account created and device provisioned.
escalationReason: Requires HR authorization and IT manager approval.

title: Data Recovery / Deleted File Recovery
description: Accidentally deleted files, need to recover data, files missing from folder
steps: Check the Recycle Bin first — restore if file is there.
Check OneDrive / SharePoint version history for cloud-synced files.
On file servers: right-click the folder → Properties → Previous Versions to restore from shadow copy.
If files were on a local drive, use Windows File History if configured.
Submit a formal data recovery request to the backup team if shadow copy fails.
Do not write new data to the disk where files were deleted (to prevent overwrite).
Escalate to L3 storage team for enterprise backup restore.
result: Data recovery in progress — backup team engaged.
escalationReason: Backup restore requires L3 storage team involvement.

title: Webcam / Microphone Not Working
description: Camera not detected, microphone not working, video call issues, Teams or Zoom no audio or video
steps: Check Device Manager for webcam/microphone errors — update or rollback drivers.
Verify app permissions: Settings → Privacy → Camera / Microphone → Allow.
Test the device in a browser-based test (webcamtests.com) to isolate OS vs app issue.
Close all other apps that may be using the camera/mic simultaneously.
In Teams/Zoom: Settings → Devices → select the correct audio/video device.
Plug external USB webcam/mic into a different USB port.
Restart the Windows Audio service: Services → Windows Audio → Restart.
result: Webcam/microphone working correctly.

title: Microsoft Teams Issues (Not Loading / Login Error)
description: Teams not starting, Teams frozen, Teams login loop, error code caa20004
steps: Sign out of Teams and sign back in.
Clear Teams cache: close Teams → delete contents of %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams.
Run Teams as Administrator.
Check Microsoft 365 service health dashboard for any outages.
Re-install Teams from the Microsoft website or IT portal.
Verify that Microsoft 365 license is assigned to the user in admin center.
Check proxy/firewall settings if the user is on a restricted network.
result: Teams client restored and user can sign in.

title: Phishing Email Reported
description: User received suspicious email, phishing attempt, email with malicious link or attachment
steps: Instruct the user NOT to click any links or download attachments from the email.
Ask user to forward the email as an attachment to the SOC mailbox: security@company.com.
Delete the email from the user's inbox immediately.
Check if the user clicked any links before reporting.
If links were clicked: isolate the machine and initiate security incident.
Submit the sender domain to the email gateway block list.
Issue a company-wide advisory if this is a widespread campaign.
result: Phishing email reported and sender blocked.
escalationReason: Security team must investigate any link-clicked incidents.

title: Hard Drive / SSD Failure
description: Disk read error, hard drive clicking noise, SSD not detected, storage failure, bad sectors
steps: Immediately run a backup of all accessible data to a network share.
Run SMART diagnostics: use CrystalDiskInfo or WMIC diskdrive get status.
Boot from a USB diagnostic tool to assess disk health outside OS.
If SMART reports critical failure, initiate hardware replacement immediately.
Escalate to hardware team with the SMART report attached.
Order a replacement drive via the procurement portal.
Re-image the machine with the user's backed-up data after replacement.
result: Hardware replacement initiated.
escalationReason: Physical hardware failure — L2 hardware team required.

title: License Expired / Activation Error (Office / Windows)
description: Microsoft Office activation error, Windows license expired, product not activated, unlicensed product
steps: Check license assignment in Microsoft 365 Admin Center → Active Users.
Re-assign the Office or Windows license if expired or removed.
On the user's machine, run: cscript slmgr.vbs /ato to force activation.
If Office: open any Office app → File → Account → Activate Product.
Ensure the machine has internet access to reach Microsoft activation servers.
If using KMS/MAK: verify the KMS server is reachable from the machine.
Restart the machine after activation.
result: License reactivated successfully.

title: USB Device Not Recognized
description: USB drive not detected, USB device not working, external hard drive not showing up
steps: Try the USB device in a different USB port.
Check Device Manager for unknown or error devices under Universal Serial Bus.
Uninstall the USB device from Device Manager and reconnect it.
Update USB host controller drivers from Device Manager.
Test the USB device on another machine to rule out device failure.
Check if USB access is restricted by company policy (GPO/DLP).
If blocked by policy: submit a data transfer request via the IT portal.
result: USB device recognized and accessible.

title: Remote Desktop (RDP) Connection Failed
description: Cannot RDP into a machine, Remote Desktop not working, RDP error code, remote access denied
steps: Verify the target machine is powered on and connected to the network.
Confirm Remote Desktop is enabled: System Properties → Remote → Allow Remote Connections.
Check Windows Firewall: ensure Remote Desktop rule is enabled (port 3389).
Verify the user is in the Remote Desktop Users group on the target machine.
Check that corporate firewall allows RDP traffic to the target subnet.
Try connecting via IP address instead of hostname.
Restart Remote Desktop Services on the target machine via services.msc.
result: RDP connection successfully established.

title: Server / Service Outage
description: Server is down, critical service unavailable, production outage, all users affected, service not responding
steps: Immediately alert the on-call infrastructure team via the incident hotline.
Open a P1 (Critical) incident ticket in the ITSM system.
Check the server status dashboard and monitoring alerts (Nagios/Datadog).
Attempt to ping and SSH/RDP into the server for diagnostics.
Review recent change management logs for any changes made in the last 24 hours.
Initiate the Business Continuity/DR plan if RTO is at risk.
Send a stakeholder communication every 30 minutes until resolution.
Post-incident: conduct a Root Cause Analysis within 48 hours.
result: Incident escalated to infrastructure team. Stakeholders notified.
escalationReason: Critical P1 outage — infrastructure and management must be engaged.

title: Unauthorized Access / Privilege Escalation Attempt
description: Unauthorized login, suspicious privilege escalation, admin access attempt, security alert
steps: Lock the affected user account immediately from Active Directory.
Notify the Security Operations Center (SOC) and CISO office.
Review authentication logs in SIEM (Splunk/Sentinel) for the time window.
Identify the source IP and block it via firewall rules.
Capture all relevant logs and preserve evidence.
Initiate the Access Control Incident Response runbook.
Conduct a full permission audit on affected systems.
If insider threat is suspected, involve HR and Legal.
result: Account locked. Security investigation in progress.
escalationReason: Security incident — SOC, CISO, and potentially Legal involvement required.

title: Dual Monitor / Display Setup Issue
description: Second monitor not detected, display resolution wrong, screen flickering, HDMI or DisplayPort not working
steps: Check physical cable connection (HDMI/DisplayPort/USB-C) at both ends.
Right-click Desktop → Display Settings → Detect → check if monitor appears.
Update display/graphics drivers from Device Manager or GPU vendor site.
Try a different cable or adapter.
Set the correct display mode: Extended, Duplicate, or Second Screen Only (Win+P).
Check monitor's own input selector button — ensure correct input is selected.
Roll back recent graphics driver update if issue appeared after an update.
result: Multi-monitor display configured correctly.

title: Employee Offboarding — Account Deprovisioning
description: Employee leaving, disable account, revoke access, offboarding, termination procedure
steps: Receive approved offboarding request from HR with last working date.
On the last working day: disable the AD account (do NOT delete immediately).
Revoke all Microsoft 365 licenses and active sessions.
Remove the user from all security groups and distribution lists.
Forward email to the line manager for 30 days.
Transfer OneDrive/SharePoint data to the manager.
Revoke VPN certificates and MFA registrations.
Document in CMDB and retain account for 90 days before deletion per policy.
result: User access fully revoked per offboarding policy.
escalationReason: Requires HR sign-off and manager approval.

title: VPN Slow / Laggy / Poor Performance
description: VPN is connected but slow, laggy, high latency, intermittent drops on VPN, poor VPN throughput, VPN performance degraded
steps: Check the VPN server load — connect to a different VPN endpoint or region if available.
Switch VPN protocol: try IKEv2 instead of OpenVPN, or vice versa, in client settings.
Enable split tunneling in VPN settings so only corporate traffic routes through VPN.
Run a speed test (speedtest.net) without VPN to rule out a local ISP issue.
Update the VPN client to the latest available version.
Adjust MTU size: set the VPN adapter MTU to 1400 to reduce packet fragmentation.
Close bandwidth-heavy applications (video streaming, large downloads) while on VPN.
If the issue persists for multiple users, notify the network team to check VPN gateway load.
result: VPN performance improved after optimization.

title: VPN Connected but Cannot Access Internal Resources
description: VPN shows connected but cannot access intranet, internal servers, or shared drives after connecting
steps: Verify the VPN client shows 'Connected' and the assigned corporate IP range.
Try to ping an internal server by IP address (not hostname) to test basic connectivity.
Flush DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns, then try accessing resources again.
Check if split tunneling is enabled — disable it temporarily to force all traffic through VPN.
Verify the user's VPN access group in the admin portal has permission for the target resource.
Re-connect VPN and check if routing table includes corporate subnets (route print).
If issue is isolated to one user, reset their VPN profile from the admin console.
result: Internal resource access restored via VPN.

title: Wi-Fi Keeps Disconnecting / Dropping
description: Wi-Fi drops intermittently, wireless connection keeps disconnecting, unstable wireless, Wi-Fi drops every few minutes
steps: Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver: Device Manager → Network Adapters → right-click → Update driver.
Disable Wi-Fi power saving: Device Manager → Network Adapter → Properties → Power Management → uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.
Change wireless band: connect to 5GHz instead of 2.4GHz (or vice versa) in network settings.
Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network.
Check for radio interference — move away from microwaves, cordless phones, and dense walls.
Run the Windows Network Troubleshooter: Settings → Network & Internet → Troubleshoot.
If issue affects multiple users, escalate to network team to check access point health.
result: Wi-Fi connection stable after driver and power settings fix.

title: Account Locked Out
description: User account is locked, too many failed login attempts, AD account locked, cannot log in due to lockout
steps: Identify the locked account in Active Directory → Search for username.
Check the lockout source: use 'Account Lockout Status' tool or Event ID 4740 in Security logs.
Identify the source machine causing repeated failed logins.
Unlock the account in AD: right-click account → Properties → Account → Unlock.
If a saved credential is causing lockouts, clear it on the source machine: Credential Manager → Windows Credentials.
Reset the password if the user has forgotten it.
Advise user to update saved passwords on all devices and apps.
result: Account unlocked and lockout source identified.

title: Permission Denied / Access Request to Resource
description: User needs access to a folder, system, or application, permission denied error, requesting access
steps: Confirm the user's business justification and manager approval for the access.
Identify the resource: shared folder, application, or system.
Check current permissions in Active Directory security groups for the resource.
Add the user to the appropriate security group with the minimum required permissions.
Test access with the user before closing.
Document the access grant in the CMDB and access control log.
Set a review date for time-limited access (if applicable).
result: Access granted after manager approval.
escalationReason: Requires manager sign-off for access to sensitive resources.

title: Zoom Issues — Cannot Join or Start Meeting
description: Zoom not connecting, cannot join meeting, Zoom error, video call not working on Zoom
steps: Check internet connection — Zoom requires at least 1.5 Mbps upload/download.
Update Zoom to the latest version from zoom.us/download.
Sign out of Zoom and sign back in.
Uninstall and reinstall Zoom if it keeps crashing.
Check firewall/proxy settings: Zoom requires ports 8801-8802 and 443.
Disable VPN temporarily to test if it is blocking Zoom.
Check Zoom service status at status.zoom.us for any outages.
result: Zoom connection restored.

title: SharePoint / OneDrive Sync Issues
description: OneDrive not syncing, SharePoint files not updating, sync errors, OneDrive stuck, cloud files not accessible
steps: Check OneDrive sync status icon in the system tray — hover to see error details.
Pause and resume sync: right-click OneDrive icon → Pause syncing → Resume syncing.
Ensure there are no file name/path issues: OneDrive does not support special characters or paths over 400 characters.
Sign out and back into OneDrive: right-click tray icon → Settings → Account → Unlink PC, then re-sign in.
Check OneDrive storage quota: if full, sync will stop.
Reset OneDrive client: run %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset.
Check SharePoint site permissions if specific library files won't sync.
result: OneDrive/SharePoint sync resumed.

title: Laptop Battery Not Charging
description: Battery not charging, laptop dies quickly, plugged in but not charging, battery health poor
steps: Check the charging cable and adapter for visible damage or loose connections.
Try a different power outlet or power strip.
Remove the battery (if removable), wait 30 seconds, reinsert and try charging.
Check battery health: open CMD → powercfg /batteryreport → review the report.
Update battery/BIOS drivers from the manufacturer's support site.
Check BIOS for battery management settings (some have threshold settings).
If the battery health report shows below 50% design capacity, raise a hardware replacement request.
result: Battery status assessed. Replacement request raised if needed.
escalationReason: Physical battery degradation may require hardware team inspection.

title: Keyboard or Mouse Not Working
description: Keyboard not responding, mouse not moving, keys stuck, wireless keyboard or mouse not pairing
steps: For wired devices: unplug and replug into a different USB port.
For wireless: replace batteries and re-pair via the USB receiver or Bluetooth.
Test the device on another machine to confirm if it is a hardware fault.
Check Device Manager for error flags on the keyboard/mouse entry.
Update HID (Human Interface Device) drivers in Device Manager.
For Bluetooth: remove the device from Bluetooth settings and re-pair.
Raise a hardware replacement request if the device is confirmed faulty.
result: Keyboard/mouse operational or replacement requested.

title: Overheating / Fan Running Loud
description: Laptop or desktop overheating, fan running at full speed constantly, device hot to touch, thermal shutdown
steps: Check Task Manager for processes running at near 100% CPU that could cause heat.
Ensure ventilation vents are not blocked — place laptop on a hard flat surface.
Use compressed air to clean dust from vents (do not open the device without authorization).
Install and run HWMonitor to check real temperature readings.
Update BIOS and chipset drivers from the manufacturer's support site.
If under warranty, raise a hardware maintenance ticket for professional cleaning.
If thermal shutdown occurs repeatedly, escalate to hardware team immediately.
result: Overheating mitigated. Hardware inspection scheduled if needed.
escalationReason: Repeated thermal shutdowns require L2 hardware team inspection.

title: Windows Update Failing / Stuck
description: Windows Update stuck, update fails with error, update loop, cannot install updates
steps: Run Windows Update Troubleshooter: Settings → Update & Security → Troubleshoot → Windows Update.
Clear update cache: stop Windows Update service → delete contents of C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution → restart service.
Run sfc /scannow and DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth in an elevated Command Prompt.
Manually download the failing update from the Microsoft Update Catalog using the KB number.
Check for disk space — Windows needs at least 10 GB free to apply major updates.
Temporarily disable antivirus during the update attempt.
If update repeatedly fails, check the Windows Update logs at C:\Windows\Logs\WindowsUpdate.
result: Windows Update completed successfully.

title: DNS Resolution Failure
description: DNS not resolving, websites not loading by name but IP works, DNS error, name resolution failure
steps: Confirm the issue: ping 8.8.8.8 (IP) — if this works, it is a DNS issue not a network issue.
Flush DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns.
Set DNS manually to 8.8.8.8 (Google) or 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare): Network Adapter Settings → IPv4 → DNS.
Check if the corporate DNS server is reachable: nslookup <server-name> <dns-server-ip>.
Restart the DNS client service: services.msc → DNS Client → Restart.
If only internal domain names fail, the corporate DNS server may be down — escalate to network team.
Reset TCP/IP stack: netsh int ip reset and netsh winsock reset, then reboot.
result: DNS resolution restored.

title: Software Update / Patch Deployment
description: Application needs to be updated, software patch required, out of date software, version upgrade request
steps: Verify the update is listed in the approved patch management schedule.
Test the update on a pilot group of machines before wide deployment.
Deploy via SCCM/Intune patch management: Software Library → Software Updates → Deploy.
Schedule the deployment outside business hours to minimize disruption.
Monitor deployment progress and check for failures in the SCCM console.
For urgent security patches, bypass the schedule and deploy immediately with manager approval.
Notify affected users of the upcoming restart requirement.
result: Patch deployed to all targeted devices.
escalationReason: Large-scale deployments require change management approval.

title: Two-Factor Authentication App Not Working
description: Authenticator app showing wrong code, OTP not accepted, 2FA not working, TOTP time sync issue
steps: Check the time on the user's phone — TOTP codes are time-based and require accurate clock.
Enable automatic time sync on the phone: Settings → Date & Time → Automatic.
In the Authenticator app, look for a 'Sync now' option in settings.
If codes still fail, remove the account from the app and re-add by scanning the QR code from the service.
If the user no longer has access to the authenticator app at all, initiate an MFA reset ticket.
Check if the account has backup codes available that can be used as a one-time bypass.
Log all MFA-related actions in the security audit trail.
result: Authenticator app synced and OTP codes working correctly.

title: ERP / Business Application Access Issue
description: Cannot access ERP system, SAP, Oracle, or business application login failing, application shows no permission
steps: Verify the user's account is active in the ERP/business application admin console.
Check that the user's role and license are correctly assigned in the application.
Clear browser cache and cookies if it is a web-based application.
Ensure the user is on the corporate network or VPN if the application requires it.
Check if the application has a separate password from Windows AD — reset if needed.
Review application-specific error logs for the user's last login attempt.
Escalate to the application owner/vendor if role assignment and connectivity are confirmed correct.
result: ERP access restored after role verification.
escalationReason: Application role changes require business owner approval.

title: Excel / Word File Won't Open or Is Corrupted
description: Excel or Word file corrupted, cannot open document, file shows error when opening, xlsx or docx file damaged
steps: Try opening the file from the original location (not a shortcut).
Use the built-in repair option: File → Open → Browse → select the file → click arrow next to 'Open' → 'Open and Repair'.
If the file is on a network share, copy it to the local desktop first, then repair.
Check SharePoint/OneDrive version history to restore an earlier uncorrupted version.
Use the online recovery tool at Word Online or Excel Online to open and re-save.
Try opening on another machine with the same Office version.
If critical data is involved, send to the vendor's file recovery service.
result: File recovered or earlier version restored.

title: Network Printer — Shared Printer Not Visible on Network
description: Network printer not showing, shared printer disappeared, printer not found on the network, cannot add network printer
steps: Verify the printer is powered on and connected to the network — check the printer's IP address from its display.
Ping the printer's IP from the user's machine to confirm network reachability.
Re-add the printer: Settings → Printers & Scanners → Add a printer or scanner → 'The printer I want isn't listed' → add by IP address.
Check if Group Policy is set to push printers — run gpupdate /force and wait for printers to appear.
Verify the print server (if applicable) is online and the shared printer is published.
Re-install the printer driver: download from manufacturer site matching the exact printer model.
Check Windows Firewall rules — File and Printer Sharing must be allowed.
result: Network printer reconnected and set as default.

title: Active Directory User Account Expired
description: AD account expired, user cannot log in because account has expired, account expiration date passed
steps: Open Active Directory Users and Computers → find the user account.
Double-click the account → Account tab → check and clear the 'Account expires' date.
Set a new appropriate expiration date or set to 'Never' per HR policy.
Unlock the account if it is also locked out.
Notify the user they can now log in.
Coordinate with HR to confirm the user's employment status before extending.
Log the change in the audit trail.
result: Account expiration resolved and user can now log in.

title: Corporate Email Account — New Setup
description: New email account needed, setting up Outlook for the first time, email not configured on device
steps: Confirm the user's email account is provisioned in Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
Open Outlook → File → Add Account → enter the corporate email address.
If auto-discover works, Outlook will configure the account automatically.
If not: manually enter Exchange server settings from the admin portal.
Assign the Microsoft 365 license including Exchange Online.
Test sending and receiving with an internal and external address.
Set up email signature and out-of-office as per company template.
result: Corporate email account configured and working.

title: Application Performance Slow / Lagging
description: Specific application is very slow, application takes long to load, software laggy, app response time high
steps: Check if the slowness is isolated to one application or system-wide.
Close other applications to free up RAM and CPU — check Task Manager.
Clear the application's cache and temporary files.
Check if the application connects to a server — test network latency to the server.
Update the application to the latest version.
Check disk health: a slow HDD can cause application loading delays.
If the application connects to a database, check database server load with the app team.
Submit a performance report to the application vendor if issue is persistent.
result: Application performance improved.

title: Projector / Meeting Room Display Not Working
description: Projector not connecting, meeting room screen blank, cannot mirror or extend to projector, HDMI to projector not working
steps: Check the projector/display is powered on and set to the correct input source.
Connect/reconnect the HDMI or VGA cable firmly at both ends.
Press Win+P and select 'Duplicate' or 'Extend' to output to the display.
Try a different cable or adapter (USB-C to HDMI if applicable).
Restart the projector and reconnect.
Update graphics drivers if the display is not detected.
Check if the meeting room AV panel has a separate input selector button.
Contact facilities if the projector itself is faulty.
result: Meeting room display connected and working.

title: Email Sending Delayed or Stuck in Outbox
description: Email stuck in outbox, emails not sending, delayed delivery, outbox not clearing
steps: Check internet and Exchange server connectivity.
Open Outlook in Online mode: File → Account Settings → Change → uncheck 'Use Cached Exchange Mode'.
Delete the stuck email from the Outbox (switch to offline mode first: Send/Receive → Work Offline).
Check if the email has a large attachment — Exchange may be blocking it for size.
Verify SMTP authentication settings if using a non-Exchange mail account.
Check if the recipient address is valid — bounce-back messages appear in the Inbox.
Repair the Outlook profile if issue persists: Control Panel → Mail → Profiles → Repair.
result: Email delivered successfully after profile repair.

title: Cannot Connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Cannot connect to office Wi-Fi, corporate wireless network not showing, 802.1X authentication failing
steps: Verify the Wi-Fi SSID is visible in the network list — if not, check if the access point is on.
Forget the corporate Wi-Fi network and reconnect from scratch.
Ensure the device is domain-joined if the corporate Wi-Fi uses 802.1X certificate auth.
Check the certificate store: the corporate root CA certificate must be installed.
Reconnect to the corporate network on Ethernet and run gpupdate /force to refresh certificates.
Check if NAC (Network Access Control) is blocking the device — look for a quarantine message.
Escalate to network team if the issue affects multiple users on the same floor/SSID.
result: Corporate Wi-Fi connection established.
escalationReason: Certificate or NAC issues require network team involvement.

title: Pop-up Ads / Browser Redirects / Adware
description: Browser showing pop-ups, random redirects, toolbar installed without consent, adware, browser hijacker
steps: Run a full Malwarebytes scan to detect and remove adware.
Reset browser settings: Chrome → Settings → Reset settings → Restore settings to original defaults.
Remove suspicious browser extensions: Chrome → Menu → More tools → Extensions.
Uninstall recently installed unknown programs from Control Panel → Programs.
Clear browser cache and cookies.
Run Windows Defender scan as a secondary check.
If issue persists after cleaning, re-image the machine to ensure full removal.
result: Adware removed and browser restored to clean state.

title: Cloud Storage Quota Exceeded
description: OneDrive or SharePoint storage full, cannot upload files, quota exceeded, storage limit reached
steps: Check current storage usage: OneDrive → Settings → Account → Manage storage.
Identify and delete large unused files or move them to an archive location.
Empty the OneDrive Recycle Bin to free immediate space.
Request a storage quota increase via the IT portal if business need justifies it.
Move old project files to the departmental SharePoint archive library.
Compress large files or use ZIP before uploading to reduce space usage.
Discuss long-term data archival policy with the user's department manager.
result: Storage space freed and sync resumed.

title: Windows Black Screen on Login
description: Black screen after login, desktop does not load, screen blank after entering password, Windows stuck on black screen
steps: Press Ctrl+Alt+Del → open Task Manager → File → Run new task → explorer.exe.
If Task Manager opens, the shell (explorer.exe) has crashed — restart it from Task Manager.
Restart the machine in Safe Mode and check if display works — rules out driver issue.
Update or roll back graphics drivers from Safe Mode.
Disable Fast Startup: Power Options → Choose what the power button does → uncheck Fast Startup.
Run sfc /scannow from Safe Mode to repair corrupted system files.
If the issue persists, perform a Startup Repair from Windows recovery environment.
result: Windows desktop restored successfully.

title: Outlook Calendar Sync / Meeting Issues
description: Calendar not syncing, meetings not showing, Outlook calendar out of date, meeting invites not received
steps: Restart Outlook and wait 2-3 minutes for calendar to sync.
Switch between Online and Cached mode: File → Account Settings → Change → toggle Cached Exchange Mode.
Delete and re-create the Outlook profile to force a fresh calendar sync.
Check the calendar folder permissions if the user is viewing a shared calendar.
Verify the Exchange server is reachable and not reporting errors in admin portal.
Compare the calendar in Outlook Web Access (OWA) — if it shows correctly there, it's a local Outlook issue.
Run the SARA (Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant) tool for automated Outlook diagnostics.
result: Outlook calendar synced and meetings visible.

title: Ransomware / Data Encryption Attack
description: Files encrypted by ransomware, ransom note found, cannot access files, ransomware attack detected
steps: IMMEDIATELY disconnect the device from ALL networks (Ethernet and Wi-Fi).
Do NOT pay the ransom or delete encrypted files.
Call the SOC incident hotline — do not use email as it may also be compromised.
Isolate all devices on the same network segment if spread is suspected.
Initiate IR-RANSOMWARE runbook — preserve all evidence.
Identify the ransomware variant using ID Ransomware tool (https://id-ransomware.malwarehunterteam.com/).
Restore affected data from the most recent clean backup after the environment is confirmed safe.
Notify executive leadership, legal, and potentially law enforcement as per GDPR/regulatory obligations.
result: Incident contained. Recovery from backup initiated.
escalationReason: Critical security incident — executive, legal, and regulatory notification required.

title: Power Outage / UPS Failure
description: Power outage in office, UPS failed, servers went down due to power loss, power supply issue
steps: Immediately notify facilities management and the infrastructure team.
Check UPS status: most enterprise UPS units have a management card accessible via IP.
Initiate graceful shutdown of non-critical servers to prevent data corruption.
Switch critical systems to generator or alternate power source if available.
Document all systems that went down with timestamps.
After power is restored, bring up systems in the correct order per the DR runbook.
Perform data integrity checks on all databases after unclean shutdown.
Raise a procurement request for UPS battery replacement if failure was battery-related.
result: Systems restored after power restoration. UPS health reviewed.
escalationReason: Facilities and infrastructure team must coordinate.

title: Database Connectivity / SQL Server Error
description: Cannot connect to database, SQL Server error, database connection timeout, application cannot reach DB
steps: Check if the SQL Server service is running: services.msc → SQL Server → verify status.
Test connectivity: telnet <db-server> 1433 or Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <db-server> -Port 1433.
Verify database credentials — password may have expired or connection string may be incorrect.
Check SQL Server error logs in SSMS or at C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\ERRORLOG.
Review firewall rules: ensure port 1433 (or named instance port) is open between the app server and DB.
Check SQL Server resource utilization — high CPU or memory may cause connection refusals.
Restart the SQL Server service if safe to do so (ensure no critical transactions are running).
result: Database connection restored.
escalationReason: Database issues require DBA involvement.

title: Cloud Service Outage (AWS / Azure / M365)
description: Cloud platform down, Azure outage, AWS service unavailable, Microsoft 365 service disruption
steps: Check the official cloud status page: Azure Status, AWS Status, or Microsoft 365 Status.
Confirm the outage is external and not a local configuration issue.
Communicate to affected users that this is a vendor outage outside IT control.
Activate Business Continuity Plan for affected services if outage is extended.
Monitor the vendor status page and subscribe to email/SMS alerts.
Document the start time, affected services, and business impact for the incident log.
Submit a formal support ticket to the cloud vendor if SLA breach is likely.
Post-incident: review cloud resilience and multi-region failover options.
result: Stakeholders notified. Monitoring vendor recovery.
escalationReason: External vendor outage — management notification required.

title: Firewall Blocking Application Traffic
description: Application cannot connect due to firewall, firewall blocking port, traffic blocked, connection refused by firewall
steps: Identify the specific port and protocol the application needs (check vendor documentation).
Test connectivity: telnet <destination> <port> or Test-NetConnection.
Check Windows Firewall rules on the local machine: Windows Defender Firewall → Advanced Settings.
Submit a firewall change request to the network team via the change management portal.
Provide business justification and the source/destination IPs and ports required.
After the rule is applied, test connectivity again and confirm with the user.
Document the firewall rule in the network asset register.
result: Firewall rule created and application traffic permitted.
escalationReason: Firewall changes require change management approval.

title: Active Directory Group Policy Not Applying
description: Group Policy not applying, GPO not working, policy settings not enforced, gpupdate failing
steps: Run gpupdate /force on the affected machine and check for errors.
Run gpresult /h gpresult.html to generate a policy result report and review it.
Verify the machine is joined to the domain: Settings → System → About → Domain.
Check if the machine can reach the domain controller: nltest /dsgetdc:<domain>.
Review the GP event log: Event Viewer → Applications and Services Logs → Microsoft → Windows → GroupPolicy.
Check the GPO link in GPMC — ensure it is linked to the correct OU and not blocked.
Verify no local policy is overriding the domain GPO: gpedit.msc → check local settings.
result: Group Policy applied successfully after investigation.
escalationReason: Domain controller connectivity issues require network team involvement.

title: Laptop Not Turning On
description: Laptop won't start, computer not powering on, no display when pressing power button, dead laptop
steps: Verify the charger is connected firmly and the power LED on the charger is on.
Try a known-good charger if available to rule out charger failure.
Perform a hard reset: hold the power button for 15 seconds, release, then press again.
Remove all external peripherals (USB, external monitor) and try powering on.
If no display but power LED is on: connect to an external monitor to rule out screen failure.
Check for any beep codes on startup — note the pattern for diagnostics.
If the laptop still does not respond, escalate to hardware team for POST-level diagnostics.
result: Laptop power issue diagnosed. Replacement or repair initiated if needed.
escalationReason: Hardware fault — L2 hardware team inspection required.

title: IT Asset Request — New Equipment
description: Requesting new laptop, monitor, keyboard, headset, or other IT hardware equipment
steps: Submit an IT hardware request form via the IT self-service portal.
Provide business justification and manager approval in the request.
Procurement team checks stock inventory and raises a purchase order if needed.
IT configures and images the new device with the standard corporate build.
Assign the asset in the CMDB under the requesting user's profile.
Arrange delivery or collection and obtain user's signature on the asset register.
Update the IT asset inventory and set next scheduled refresh date.
result: Equipment ordered or assigned from stock.
escalationReason: Procurement and manager approval required for new hardware.

title: Remote Work Setup Issues
description: Cannot work from home, home office setup not connecting, remote working connectivity problems
steps: Confirm the user's home internet is working by testing a non-corporate website.
Ensure VPN client is installed — download from the IT software portal if not.
Connect to VPN using corporate credentials and verify connection status.
Test access to internal resources (email, intranet, shared drives) over VPN.
If using a corporate laptop, ensure it is not in an offline/disconnected state for too long — rejoin domain if needed.
Check if the corporate device firewall is blocking home network traffic.
Provide IT helpdesk home support contact details for out-of-hours assistance.
result: Remote work connectivity established.

title: SSO (Single Sign-On) Not Working
description: Single sign-on failing, SSO error, SAML authentication error, cannot log into application with corporate account
steps: Clear browser cookies and cache, then retry SSO.
Ensure the user is logged into their corporate account in the browser.
Check if the browser is blocking third-party cookies — allow them for the SSO domain.
Verify the user's account is active in the identity provider (Azure AD / Okta / ADFS).
Check if the application's SAML configuration is correct in the IdP admin portal.
Try an incognito browser window to rule out browser extension interference.
Check the IdP audit logs for the specific error code and share with the app owner.
result: SSO authentication working after browser and IdP verification.

title: Backup Failure / Backup Not Running
description: Backup job failing, backup not completing, backup software error, scheduled backup missed
steps: Check the backup software console for error messages and job logs.
Verify the backup destination storage has sufficient free space.
Confirm the backup service account credentials have not expired.
Check network connectivity between the backup agent and the backup server.
Retry the backup job manually and monitor for completion.
Review the backup schedule — ensure there are no resource conflicts with other jobs.
Alert the storage/backup team if the failure has persisted for more than one cycle.
result: Backup job restarted and completing successfully.
escalationReason: Extended backup failure requires immediate storage team attention.

title: Screen Flickering / Display Artifacts
description: Screen flickering, random screen flashing, display artifacts, horizontal lines on screen, monitor glitching
steps: Check the refresh rate: right-click Desktop → Display Settings → Advanced display settings — set to recommended rate.
Update graphics drivers from Device Manager or GPU vendor site.
Try a different cable (HDMI/DisplayPort) or a different port on the GPU.
Test with a different monitor to determine if the issue is with the GPU or the monitor.
Roll back graphics drivers if flickering started after a recent driver update.
Check for electromagnetic interference — move speakers or power supplies away from the monitor.
If the screen flickers in BIOS/Safe Mode, the issue is hardware — escalate to hardware team.
result: Display stabilized after driver update or cable replacement.
escalationReason: Hardware-level flickering (BIOS-stage) requires L2 hardware inspection.

title: Cannot Send Large Email Attachments
description: Email attachment size limit, cannot send large files via email, attachment rejected, file too large to email
steps: Inform the user of the email attachment limit (typically 25 MB for Exchange/M365).
Upload the file to OneDrive or SharePoint and share a link instead of an attachment.
Use the 'Attach as link' option in Outlook when attaching files from OneDrive.
For very large files, use the approved secure file transfer service (e.g., ShareFile, WeTransfer Business).
Compress the file to ZIP format to reduce size if just under the limit.
For recurring large file sharing needs, set up a SharePoint document library with external sharing.
result: User guided to use OneDrive link sharing as an alternative.

title: BIOS / Firmware Update Required
description: BIOS update needed, firmware out of date, system stability issues related to BIOS version
steps: Identify the current BIOS version: System Information (msinfo32) → BIOS Version.
Go to the manufacturer's support site and check for the latest BIOS version.
Download the BIOS update utility from the manufacturer.
Ensure the laptop/PC is plugged into power before starting the BIOS update.
Run the BIOS update utility and follow the on-screen instructions — do NOT interrupt the process.
Machine will restart several times during the update — this is normal.
Verify the new BIOS version in msinfo32 after the update completes.
result: BIOS updated successfully.
escalationReason: BIOS updates carry risk — should be done by trained IT staff.

title: User Reporting IT Security Policy Violation
description: Reporting a coworker for policy violation, suspicious activity by another employee, insider threat report
steps: Receive the report confidentially and document the allegation with dates and details.
Do NOT confront the accused employee — preserve the confidentiality of the report.
Notify the Information Security team and HR simultaneously.
Pull access logs and audit trails for the accused account discreetly.
Preserve all evidence per the legal hold policy.
Initiate an investigation under the Acceptable Use Policy framework.
If immediate risk is identified, restrict the account pending investigation.
Keep the reporting employee informed of the process without disclosing investigation details.
result: Security investigation initiated. HR and InfoSec notified.
escalationReason: HR, Legal, and InfoSec must all be involved per policy.

title: Scanner Not Working
description: Scanner not detected, cannot scan documents, scanner software error, scan to email not working
steps: Check the scanner is powered on and USB/network cable is connected.
In Windows: Settings → Devices → check if the scanner appears; if not, install drivers.
Download the correct scanner driver from the manufacturer's website.
For network scanners: verify the scanner's IP is pingable and scan-to-email settings are configured.
Test with Windows Scan app (from the Microsoft Store) as a basic scan test.
For 'scan to email' issues: check SMTP relay configuration on the scanner's web UI.
Restart the Windows Image Acquisition (WIA) service: services.msc → Windows Image Acquisition → Restart.
result: Scanner operational after driver installation.

title: Two-Step Verification / Login Prompt Loop
description: Repeated MFA prompts, stuck in login loop, authentication not completing, MFA keeps asking again and again
steps: Clear browser cookies and cached credentials for the site.
Check if the 'Remember this device' option is being blocked by a browser policy.
In Azure AD / Okta: review Conditional Access policies — the user's device may not be compliant.
Enroll the device in Microsoft Intune/MDM if Conditional Access requires a compliant device.
Check if the user's session tokens have been revoked — re-authenticate from a fresh browser.
If using a personal device: ensure the browser supports modern authentication.
Escalate to Identity team if Conditional Access policy adjustment is required.
result: Login loop resolved after compliance check.

title: Telephone / VoIP Phone Not Working
description: Desk phone not working, VoIP phone offline, cannot make or receive calls, IP phone offline
steps: Check the phone's network cable — VoIP phones use PoE (Power over Ethernet).
Reboot the phone by unplugging and replugging the network cable.
Verify the phone's IP address and that it can reach the VoIP server (PBX/UCaaS).
Check the VoIP admin portal for the extension registration status.
Re-provision the phone from the UCaaS admin console.
If the phone powers on but shows 'Unregistered', check SIP credentials in the phone's web UI.
Escalate to the telephony team if the server or SIP trunk is causing the issue.
result: VoIP phone registered and calls working.

title: Web Browser Issues — Not Loading Pages
description: Browser not loading pages, websites timing out, browser crashing, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, can't browse
steps: Test a different browser to isolate whether the issue is browser-specific or system-wide.
Clear the browser cache and cookies: Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data.
Disable browser extensions one by one to find one causing issues.
Reset browser settings to default.
Check proxy settings: browser → Settings → Advanced → System → Open proxy settings.
Flush DNS: ipconfig /flushdns and retry.
Uninstall and reinstall the browser if it is crashing repeatedly.
result: Browser loading pages correctly after reset.

title: IT Compliance — Encryption Not Enabled (BitLocker)
description: BitLocker not enabled, device encryption off, compliance failure for unencrypted drive, need to enable disk encryption
steps: Check BitLocker status: Control Panel → BitLocker Drive Encryption → check C: drive status.
Enable BitLocker via Intune: push the encryption policy from Intune Endpoint Security.
If enabling manually: Control Panel → BitLocker → Turn on BitLocker → choose TPM method.
Save the recovery key to Active Directory: use Backup-BitLockerKeyProtector PowerShell command.
Verify TPM chip is enabled and initialized: tpm.msc.
Monitor encryption progress — it runs in the background and may take hours on a full drive.
Confirm encryption status in Microsoft Endpoint Manager compliance dashboard.
result: BitLocker encryption enabled and recovery key backed up to AD.
escalationReason: Encryption enablement requires administrative rights and TPM verification.

title: Application Access Denied After System Migration
description: User cannot access application after PC replacement or system migration, access that worked before now fails
steps: Verify the new device is domain-joined and the user has logged in with domain credentials.
Re-map network drives as these are not migrated automatically.
Re-install applications that are device-licensed rather than user-licensed.
Re-sync application credentials: clear Windows Credential Manager saved passwords.
Re-enroll the device in Intune/MDM if Conditional Access is blocking it as non-compliant.
Re-activate any locally-installed software licenses.
Test access to all critical applications and document any outstanding issues.
result: Application access restored on the new device.

title: IT Self-Service Portal Access Issues
description: Cannot access IT portal, self-service portal not loading, ITSM tool error, service desk portal down
steps: Check if the portal is accessible from another browser or device.
Clear browser cache and try again.
Verify the portal URL — ensure no typo and it is on the correct domain.
Check if the user's account has access to the self-service portal (some portals require explicit user onboarding).
Check if the ITSM platform is experiencing an outage — check the vendor status page.
Try logging in via the admin backdoor URL if the self-service portal is down.
Raise the incident via phone or email as a workaround while the portal is down.
result: Self-service portal access restored.

title: Sophos / CrowdStrike / Antivirus Agent Not Running
description: Antivirus agent offline, endpoint protection not active, security agent not running, AV service stopped
steps: Check the antivirus service in services.msc — start it if stopped.
Open the antivirus console and check for error messages.
Re-register the agent with the management console if it shows as offline.
Uninstall and reinstall the endpoint agent using the deployment package from the security portal.
Ensure the device has internet access to reach the security cloud (required for Sophos/CrowdStrike).
Check if Windows Defender is conflicting — only one primary AV should be active.
Escalate to the security team if the agent cannot be registered after reinstall.
result: Endpoint security agent restored and reporting to management console.

title: Slow Login / Profile Loading Slowly
description: Windows login takes very long, user profile loading slow, long time to reach desktop after entering password
steps: Check if the Group Policy is taking long to apply at login: Event Viewer → Microsoft → Windows → GroupPolicy.
Disable unnecessary startup applications via Task Manager → Startup tab.
Check if the roaming profile or folder redirection is the cause — measure network speed at login.
Run gpupdate /force to ensure clean group policy application.
Delete and recreate the local profile cache if corrupted: System → Advanced System Settings → User Profiles.
Check if Antivirus is scanning at login — configure exclusion for the user profile path.
If domain login is slow: check the domain controller response time with nltest.
result: Login time reduced after profile and startup optimization.

title: Exchange / Email Server Down
description: Email server not responding, Exchange server down, cannot send or receive any emails, all users email affected
steps: Immediately open a P1 incident ticket and notify the infrastructure team.
Check Exchange Server health in the Exchange Admin Center or via Test-ServiceHealth PowerShell.
Attempt to connect to the Exchange server via RDP for direct diagnostics.
Review Exchange event logs: Event Viewer → Application → look for MSExchange errors.
Check disk space on Exchange server — full disks cause Exchange to stop accepting mail.
Restart Exchange transport services if they have stopped.
Communicate to all users via an alternate channel (phone/Teams/SMS) that email is affected.
result: Exchange server recovered. Email flow restored.
escalationReason: All-user email outage — P1 incident with infrastructure team.

title: SLA Breach Warning — Ticket Approaching Deadline
description: SLA breach imminent, ticket approaching resolution deadline, escalation required due to time
steps: Immediately review the ticket's current status and remaining SLA time.
Contact the assigned engineer for a status update.
If blocked, escalate to the team lead for immediate assistance.
Notify the customer/user of the delay and provide a revised ETA.
If the ticket requires input from another team, escalate with explicit SLA deadline noted.
Update the ticket with all actions taken and current status.
After resolution, conduct a brief post-incident review to prevent future SLA breaches.
result: Ticket resolved within extended SLA window after escalation.
escalationReason: SLA breach risk — immediate escalation to team lead required.

title: Conference Room AV System Not Working
description: Meeting room AV not working, conference room display blank, room audio system failing, video conferencing system offline
steps: Power cycle all AV equipment in the room (display, codec, audio bar).
Check all cable connections behind the AV controller or wall plate.
Verify the AV control panel/touch screen is responsive.
Test a direct laptop connection via HDMI to the display to isolate the AV system.
For Teams Rooms/Zoom Rooms: restart the room PC and check the Teams Rooms app loads.
Check if the room is registered in the meeting room admin console (Teams Admin Center).
Contact the AV vendor support if room-level hardware components are faulty.
result: Meeting room AV system operational.
escalationReason: Dedicated AV hardware issues may require vendor on-site support.

title: Domain Join / Computer Account Issues
description: Computer cannot join domain, trust relationship failed, machine account error, computer not in AD
steps: Check network connectivity to the domain controller: nltest /dsgetdc:<domain>.
For 'trust relationship failed': disjoin and rejoin the domain.
To rejoin: System → Rename this PC (Advanced) → Member of: WORKGROUP → restart → rejoin domain.
Use a local admin account to perform the domain rejoin.
Ensure the machine account in AD is not disabled — check in ADUC.
If using Autopilot/Intune: verify the device is registered in the Intune portal.
After rejoining, run gpupdate /force and verify Group Policy applies correctly.
result: Machine successfully rejoined to the domain.
escalationReason: Domain join requires IT admin credentials.
